theorem_title: From admissible sharp-tail parameters to the shared 3SUM specification
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSumSharpTail.admissible_parameters_solve_3sum
    (c : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) (a s r : ℚ) (hc : 10 < c)
    (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ9 : θ < 9 / 10)
    (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hs0 : 0 < s) (hs1 : s < 1)
    (henc : (a : ℝ) * (ThreeSumSharpTail.encodingExponent c + ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ) < 1)
    (hprep : (s : ℝ) < ThreeSumSharpTail.sharpSaving c θ)
    (hquery : (s : ℝ) < 1 / 2 - ThreeSumSharpTail.queryExponent θ)
    (hprime : Real.log 7 / Real.log 2 + 3 * (a : ℝ) / 2 < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hbuild : 2 + (a : ℝ) * (1 + (s : ℝ) / 2) < 3 - (a : ℝ) * s / 2)
    (hr : 2 - a * s / 4 < r) :
    EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $c>10$ be an integer, $0<\theta<0.9$, and let $a,s,r$ be rational with $0<a<1$ and $0<s<1$. Suppose
$$a(A(c)+\gamma_*(c,\theta))<1,\qquad s<\gamma_*(c,\theta),\qquad s<\tfrac12-q(\theta),$$
$$\log_2 7+\tfrac32a<3-as/2,\qquad 2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2,\qquad r>2-as/4.$$
Then deterministic integer 3SUM satisfies the campaign's exact shared predicate `EndStatement.ThreeSum.SolvedInTime r`. This is the combined consequence of Propositions 4.1 and 5.1, not a verbatim separate proposition in the manuscript. Its proof must construct the word-RAM program and establish correctness and all costs using the inherited algorithms and reductions. No inner-algorithm oracle or correctness assumption is supplied as a hypothesis. The uniform word-width requirement in the shared specification is part of the formalization obligation.

readback.readback: For every natural number $c$, real number $\theta$, and rational numbers $a,s,r$, assume $c>10$, $0<\theta<9/10$, $0<a<1$, and $0<s<1$. Define $H(x)=-x\log x-(1-x)\log(1-x)$, with the total real logarithm taking value $0$ at zero and the logarithm of the absolute value at negative arguments, $S=[cH(1/c)-cH((1-\theta)/c)-\theta\log9]/\log4$, $Q=[H(\theta)+\theta\log9]/\log4$, and $E=[c\log10-cH(1/c)/2-(c-1)\log3]/\log4$. Also assume the five strict real inequalities $a(E+S)<1$, $s<S$, $s<1/2-Q$, $\log7/\log2+3a/2<3-as/2$, and $2+a(1+s/2)<3-as/2$, where natural and rational parameters are cast to the reals, together with the strict rational inequality $2-as/4<r$. The conclusion is the following quantified assertion about a specified machine: for every natural number $\kappa$, there exist a finite instruction list $P$, a natural number $b$, a function $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and a natural number $K$ such that $T(n)^q\le K n^{\max(p,0)}$ for every natural $n\ge2$, where $r=p/q$ is the reduced rational representation with integer numerator $p$ and positive natural denominator $q$. For every natural $n$, every integer sequence $(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ satisfying $|x_i|\le n^\kappa$ at every position, and every natural word width $W\ge b(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$, with the integer logarithm taken to be $0$ at $n=0$, running this same $P$ from instruction position $0$ halts within $T(n)$ steps with acceptance if and only if there exist three pairwise distinct positions $i,j,k$ in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with $x_i+x_j+x_k=0$ as integers. Memory consists of $W$-bit words at all integer addresses; initially address $0$ contains $n$ modulo $2^W$, addresses $1$ through $n$ contain the corresponding inputs modulo $2^W$, and every other address contains zero. An instruction may write the constant $1$ to a fixed integer address, add, subtract, or multiply words at two fixed addresses into another fixed address modulo $2^W$, load through an address read as a signed word, store through an address read as a signed word, jump to a specified natural instruction position if a fixed cell is negative when read as a signed word, accept, or reject. Indirect load writes into a fixed cell; indirect store reads its source from a fixed cell. Each instruction takes one step, writing proceeds to the next instruction, a non-taken conditional branch also proceeds to the next instruction, and executing beyond the finite list rejects. A halting instruction counts toward the time bound; with zero steps there is no verdict. There is no further condition on the final memory. The witnesses may depend on $\kappa$ and the initially fixed parameters but must work uniformly for every eligible $n$, input, and $W$, with no upper bound on $W$. The correctness requirement includes $n=0,1,2$, for which no three distinct positions exist and the verdict must be rejection; the polynomial inequality only constrains $n\ge2$. For $n=0$ the input magnitude condition is vacuous, and natural powers use $0^0=1$. The definition does not require $b>0$ or $K>0$, so if a chosen $b$ is zero the quantifier includes zero-width words. Under the parameter hypotheses $r>7/4$, so the numerator truncation in the time bound does not alter $p$. No claim is made for parameter choices failing any hypothesis, and no upper bound on $r$ is imposed.
